event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: COVID-19 is treated by Aon as a recent, already-felt shock that remains capable of materially distorting future performance.  The filing, dated February 2022, is well within the 0-3-year ‘recent-event’ window, so the Time Decay Principle allows high risk scores.  The company explicitly states that: (i) its 2021 results were already ‘adversely affected’; (ii) numerous operational and financial vectors—credit-market access, client demand, E&O claims, workforce health, remote-work controls—could further erode performance; and (iii) the breadth of impacts spans every geography and business line.  Although management cites mitigants (vaccination progress, phased office re-entry, business-continuity protocols, and some recovery of results in late-2021), these do not neutralise the pervasive, multi-channel risks described.  The disclosures are mostly qualitative and unquantified, yet they link the pandemic directly to realised margin pressure and to a long inventory of forward-looking threats.  Accordingly, the overall risk profile is high-to-severe, warranting elevated snippet scores that nonetheless reflect any explicit mitigating language.

evidence_list.snippet: Economic downturns, volatility, or uncertainty in the broader economy or in specific markets (including as a result of endemics or pandemics, climate change, political unrest, or otherwise) may cause reductions in technology and discretionary spending by our clients, which may result in reductions in the growth of new business or reductions in existing business.

components.reason: Links pandemics to reduced client spending and slower business growth (direct business impact).
Language is conditional ('may cause'), signalling uncertainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides a clear but generic pathway from pandemics to revenue loss; uncertainty tempers the score.

evidence_list.snippet: These losses may be attributable in whole or in part to failures on our part or to events entirely outside of our control, including but not limited to uncertainty or volatility in financial markets due to economic, political, and regulatory conditions or pandemics.

components.reason: Explicitly names pandemics as a driver of financial-market volatility that could create losses.
Presented as a potential, not a realised, impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Acknowledges pandemic risk to investment outcomes, but only in possibility terms, yielding a modest score.

evidence_list.snippet: Our results of operations have been adversely affected and could be materially adversely affected in the future by the COVID-19 global pandemic.

components.reason: States an actual adverse impact already realised.
Warns of future 'material' adverse effects (severity).
Strong wording ('materially adversely').

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Combines realised damage with a warning of material future harm, justifying a very high score.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 global pandemic and the emergence of COVID-19 variants has created significant public health concerns and significant volatility, uncertainty, and economic disruption in every region where we operate.

components.reason: Describes wide-ranging, already-occurred disruption across all regions.
Highlights continuing volatility and uncertainty due to variants.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows pervasive current impact and evolving threat; high but not maximum because still qualitative.

evidence_list.snippet: A number of evolving factors related to the global pandemic and the post-pandemic recovery period may influence the duration, nature and extent of the impact on our business and financial results.

components.reason: Signals multiple, shifting variables that could prolong harm.
Future-oriented and unquantified, adding uncertainty rather than hard impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Captures breadth and uncertainty of potential future impacts; mid-high severity.

evidence_list.snippet: Such factors include worldwide macroeconomic conditions, including interest rates, employment rates, consumer confidence and spending, gross domestic product, property values, and changes in client behavior, and foreign exchange rates in each of the markets in which we operate; business closures; changes in laws, regulations (including those changes that may provide for extended premium payment terms), and guidance; court decisions and litigation trends; a decline in business and the ability of counterparties to pay for our services on time or at all; an increased number of E&O claims in those areas impacted by the pandemic, as well as an increase in the incidence or severity of E&O claims against us and our market partners; our ability to sell and provide our services, including due to the impact of travel restrictions, lockdowns, quarantines, social distancing, and alternative work arrangements; the health of, and the effect of the pandemic on, our employees; political disruption; potential effects on our internal controls and risk mitigation processes, including those over financial reporting, as a result of changes in working environments for our employees and business partners; resurgences of spread; identification of new, more contagious variants of the virus; resulting “lockdowns,” government restrictions, mandates, requirements or recommendations; and uncertainties in vaccine adoption.

components.reason: Lists multiple concrete operational and financial risk channels (business closures, E&O claims, workforce health, travel restrictions).
Demonstrates complexity and breadth of potential impacts.
Covers emerging issues like variants and vaccine uptake, showing ongoing uncertainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highly detailed enumeration of diverse, significant risk vectors merits a near-peak score.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, the continuing COVID-19 pandemic may again create significant disruptions or volatility in the credit or financial markets, or impact our credit ratings, which could adversely affect our ability to access capital on favorable terms or at all.

components.reason: Identifies potential disruption to financing ability and credit ratings (material corporate finance risk).
Presented as a possibility ('may again'), not yet realised.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Flags a serious but still contingent capital-markets risk, deserving a moderate-high score.

evidence_list.snippet: Finally, the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic may heighten other risks discussed in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, and stock price.

components.reason: Connects pandemic to amplification of all other corporate risks and financial metrics.
Conditional language ('may heighten'), general rather than specific.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows broad systemic amplification of risk, yet remains generic, hence a mid-range score.

evidence_list.snippet: The outbreak of the coronavirus, which causes COVID-19, was declared by the World Health Organization to be a pandemic and has impacted almost all countries, in varying degrees, creating significant public health concerns, and significant volatility, uncertainty, and economic disruption in every region in which we operate.

components.reason: Acknowledges actual global impact on all operating regions.
Emphasises volatility and economic disruption.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Confirms global scope and realised disruption, supporting a robust score.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has resulted, and may continue to result, in significant economic disruption and volatility, although in recent months progress has been made in the development and distribution of vaccines, contributing to overall improved economic conditions globally, despite recent developments as a result of the Delta and Omicron variants.

components.reason: States ongoing and potential future disruption and volatility.
Notes mitigating factor of vaccine progress and some improvement.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Balances acknowledged disruption with vaccine mitigation, lowering the net severity.

evidence_list.snippet: We continue to closely monitor the situation and its impacts on our business, liquidity, and capital planning initiatives.

components.reason: Shows active monitoring, indicating ongoing concern.
Monitoring represents a mitigation effort.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Purely a mitigation statement; risk impact neutralised to zero.

evidence_list.snippet: We continue to be fully operational and to reoccupy certain offices in phases, where deemed appropriate and in compliance with governmental restrictions considering the impact on health and safety of our colleagues, their families, and our clients, and we have restricted or minimized access to offices where appropriate to support the health and safety of our colleagues.

components.reason: Implies operational disruption requiring phased re-entry and restrictions.
Highlights health-and-safety mitigations reducing risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Operational adjustments are balanced by mitigation, yielding a neutral net score.

evidence_list.snippet: We continue to deploy business continuity protocols to facilitate remote working capabilities to ensure the health and safety of our colleagues and to comply with public health and travel guidelines and restrictions.

components.reason: References remote-work protocols, evidencing ongoing operational disruption.
Describes proactive mitigation (business-continuity protocols).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Again, mitigation offsets the operational impact, resulting in a neutral score.

evidence_list.snippet: As the situation continues to evolve, the scale and duration of disruption cannot be predicted, and it is not possible to quantify or estimate the full impact that COVID-19 will have on our business.

components.reason: Emphasises unpredictability and inability to quantify impact, signalling high uncertainty.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights deep uncertainty without mitigation or quantification, meriting a moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: While we continue to focus on managing our cash flow to meet liquidity needs, our results of operations, particularly with respect to our more discretionary revenues, may be adversely affected.

components.reason: Warns of potential adverse effect on discretionary revenue streams.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Pinpoints vulnerable revenue segments; clear but unquantified risk leads to a mid-level score.

evidence_list.snippet: However, for the year ended December 31, 2021, the impacts of COVID-19 on our business results have lessened and we have seen overall strength across the firm.

components.reason: Acknowledges easing of pandemic impact—a mitigating signal.
Still recognises that the pandemic previously affected results (historical impact).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Predominantly a mitigation statement, producing a negative net score that is floored at zero by the scoring rules.
